utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While I read, the registrar can fetch the witness. Regarding the admission of evidence through the witness Muamer Tokic. The Chamber will pronounce itself regarding the admissibility of the evidence during the appearance of the witness on the 30th of October. The Chamber admits 2D 00205 submitted by the Defence on the grounds that it has certain probative value and a certain relevance. The Chamber recalls that document P 01413 and P 01636 submitted by the Prosecution were already admitted into evidence on the 27th of October, 2006.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oral decision with respect to the admission of documents concerning the testimony of Zijada Kurbegovic, and the Chamber will render its decision with respect to the documents submitted through this witness on the 26th of October. The documents were submitted by the Prosecution and the Defence, and they will admit them because they have probative value and relevance. P 01027, 3D 00464 and 476. The Chamber wishes to recall that the document P 07350 was already admitted on the 30th of October. We shall now continue the proceedings with a view to completing the cross-examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. In the transcript the legal officer tells me that there was an error in line 7, page 3, it says 476 -- 3D 00476. Mr. Praljak will complete his cross-examination, and I give him the floor with satisfaction. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examination by the Accused Praljak: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Brigadier Agic. Let us continue our work. Could we see Exhibit P 00840. I think we can cover these documents quite quickly and then we will have some comments to make. Mr. Agic, it is a record by Colonel Miro Andric which he addressed to me. It says on the document "for General Praljak."

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am unable to find it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Never mind. This is just my introduction. It will appear later on, and you will be able to look at what it contains and what the aims were at that time in that territory. P 00840. You have the document now?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you quickly look at it. He was given an order to take over the coordination and command with a view to achieving a Joint Command. He was not the commander of the Joint Command but for the purpose of a Joint Command of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the HVO, and I will read for you a part of this document. "The first level of coordination has been achieved without ignoring the agreement achieved. "It is a bit difficult to achieve agreement because the armed forces of Bugojno are getting instructions from Zenica which do not coincide with the agreement on Joint Command. Also, the curfew has been introduced and joint patrolled by the military police, and there is goodwill to implement this." He is referring to Bugojno. "The coordination is showing positive progress, but the HVO of Bugojno will be able to raise the level of alert required for an attack. Agreement has been reached on the method and easier passage of convoys and other vehicles towards Bugojno, Zenica, and Tuzla. There are certain problems in Prozor which you are already familiar with. As for your command regarding separation of opposing forces of the HVO and the armed forces at Makljen, I wish to inform you that regarding the order for the withdrawal of units from Ravno on the 24th of November, together with Fahrudin Agic, he personally withdrew the 2nd Battalion from the Crni Vrh and the quarter 1013 -- 1303." Mr. Agic goes on to inform him that he has withdrawn his units from the mentioned region, et cetera. However, he says: "According to my order for the closure of catering institutions at 1500 hours, the HVO is respecting the order whereas the armed forces of Gornji Vakuf will not respect the order because Mr. Agic says that his superior command is in Zenica, and when he receives an order from them he will carry it out." Do you know that in those days because of the bad influence of catering establishments we managed to impose a curfew in Bugojno, Novi Travnik, but we didn't manage to achieve that in Gornji Vakuf. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I don't think that there was any need to introduce your curfew, and as the commander of the Municipal Staff of Gornji Vakuf did not have the authority to close civilian facilities, catering facilities. They bothered me, too, but that was a problem for the authorities in Gornji Vakuf. It wasn't a problem only in Gornji Vakuf. Gornji Vakuf was not proclaimed a war zone for the command to be able to regulate life and work in the municipality. There were civilian authorities and police authorities, and it is their duty and competence to close catering institutions. Furthermore, Mr. Andric that you mention, we did discuss this problem and in his report I see that he -- he seems to write in a tone of a superior officer. General, you know that was the problem. It wasn't up to Fahrudin Agic. Mr. Mato Andric did not have the competencies to issue orders to the armed forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina or the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Agic, I didn't say that he did. This is about a coordination of efforts. It functioned in Bugojno. It was simply an attempt to address the problems, and one of those problems, a very major problem, I hope you will agree with me, was the fact that people who were not on the front lines and who took their weapons home with them without any control would go to inns and bars and provoke a lot of trouble, the greatest amount of trouble. I hope you will agree with me in saying that that was one of the main causes of so many incidents and killings on both sides. Would you agree with this part of my question?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. But Mr. Andric, in the part of the report that you have just read, in the first paragraph he says, "My order to close." Neither he nor I could order such a thing. The part of the town that was controlled and managed by the HVO, they dealt with it in that way. I did not have the competence as commander of the territorial staff, nor could the brigade commander. We had a lot of difficulty with the authorities. I didn't like it either, General.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me --

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Will you let me please explain this first. Before this there was a killing of an invalid in Gornji Vakuf, Rajic Pero Vlatko. I know him as we were born in the same village. He slaughtered a man. Miro Andric promised to deal with it, and that man reappeared in Gornji Vakuf shortly after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not interrupting you to prevent you from telling us about this, but this is a problem that the Court has already been informed about this. That is why I interrupted you so that we wouldn't waste any more time. But never mind. The fact remains that in the opinion of Mr. Andric and following my instructions more should have been done with the civilian authorities. I understand that you were awaiting Zenica to react, but in the meantime the problems increased. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we look at the next exhibit now. Number 14. 3D 00510.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I have 511. I don't have 510. I found 3D 00511. I don't have 3D 510.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go back, then, please, to 3D 00506. 3D 00506 until we find this other document. It's been found. Let's go back then to 3D 00 -- it is another report by Mr. Andric, a part of a lengthier report that he submitted. Have you got this report?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the screen I have an order dated the 12th of January.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, the report. 3D 00506. 3D 00506. It's a report. It says: "I have established contact with HVO commanders and of the commanders of the BiH forces." He lists the names. He says: "The HVO in Bugojno have immediately taken steps and have achieved good fortified lines. The armed forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina," that is the armija, "is showing interest in cooperation and are working on the fortification of positions. The relations with Senad Dautovic have been established. He's ready to cooperate and the agreement is being respected."

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you move the document up?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the end he reproaches you and says: "Commander Fahrudin Agic is not showing any interest in cooperation, and whenever any agreement is reached -- both Dautovic and you are in the 3rd Corps. So according to Mr. Andric's report cooperation is excellent with a part of the leadership, but he says regarding you that you're endeavouring to avoid implementing the decisions. And in the report it goes on to say that the superiors should bring pressure to bear on Mr. Agic for him to show a willingness to cooperate and to abide by agreements achieved. Tell us, what were the misunderstandings between you and Mr. Andric?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You keep implying that I was obstructive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not I. I'm just reading the report. Would you please try and explain this report which I and the HVO received from Andric?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General, you held a meeting on the 4th of November in Gornji Vakuf, and after that meeting these measures were supposed to be implemented -- to have been implemented; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were going to implement what you decided at the joint commission. Within that framework, some of the check-points which were uni-ethnic should have been disbanded, the Sebesic road and check-point and the Makljen check-point was never disband, and you know that full well, better than me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not from Banac [as interpreted] but I thought Sebesic -- no, Cabanac held that position. I don't know what commanded with him there, but he did that separately. We followed orders and complied with what had been agreed upon and signed, but I as the commander of the Municipal Staff Bugojno Vakuf never received an order to be subordinated in completing my assignments to the unit that was commanded by the HVO. And what it says here is not right. You know that at that time we had another meeting up there. We enhanced the line. You know that we connected it up, linked it up, and I don't know where this observation comes from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nor do I. I'm just reading it. Let's move on. May I now have P 00112. P 001112 is the next document I'd like to show the witness. And the date is the 12th of January, 1993. It is a regular combat report of the operative zone of north-western Herzegovina, and under A, information about the enemy, referring to the army of Republika Srpska. And it says there that the possibility exists -- there is the possibility that in the area of Gornji Vakuf, in the broader area of Gornji Vakuf, the enemy, and in brackets, the Chetniks might have opened fire because we noted an order from Banja Luka issued to the commander at Kupres. Is that what it says there? That is to say, the Serbs obviously knew about the misunderstandings and tried to use it to their own benefit. Do we agree there? Is that what it says? Were you certain at that time that every shell -- or, rather, let me put it this way: Was Vakuf shelled from Republika Srpska territory before?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only in July. Once, when the town was shelled, 18 projectiles fell on the town, in fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, I want at that ask you: Can Republika Srpska target Vakuf? Was that possible?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you always certain when something was targeted, some projectile except for mortars, which we knew couldn't go there, were you certain that it was the HVO or could the shell have come from the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only in one case were we accused of being targeted at Pidris with 22 projectiles, and Mr. Andric was wounded on that occasion. I think that that was on the 18th and 19th of January, and I'm sure you remember that. And they opened fire with the 122-millimetre howitzers down there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. May I have the next document, please. It is number 14. Document 0 -- 3D 00510. 510. 3D 00510.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't got that document in my files. Yes, I have it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, think what it says in the first sentence: "Peacefully," and we're talking about the 12th of January, 1993, by peaceful means he is issuing an order, Colonel Siljeg is issuing an order, "free our arrested on" -- according to the principle of all for all. So the Gornji Vakuf Brigade it is quite obvious that the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina has some captured HVO members, and he says -- do we agree that -- that it says: "Our men captured should be released by peaceful means on the principle of all for all. Our forces should be held under control, not to engage in provocations and not to provoke first. Follow the situation. As for the Voljevac-Gornji Vakuf axis, you have forces from the village of Dobrosin. Ensure that you have communications with them and regulate this engagement if the need arises. We managed to obtain some intelligence information, according to which the Chetniks were ordered to strike the Muslim village with one weapon and the Croatian village with another to give the impression that it was -- is the Croats that opened fire on the Muslims, or vice versa the Muslims opened fire on the Croats." Is that what it says there?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we now have the next document, P 001101, P 01101. Is it a report?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. It is a report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once again, Colonel Miroslav Andric, the date is the 12th of January, 1993, and the report for the operative zone of North-west Herzegovina. We'll skip the fact that there were problems and complications around Christmas. And it says: "The problems with the army are becoming more complicated and culminating in Gornji Vakuf when Croatian [indiscernible] have been taken out of and there is gradual deployment of soldiers along with the BH army and that check-points were established in town, around the town, and especially towards Prozor. Tensions have grown and they have almost reached a climax. Explosive -- an explosive was planted in the Radusa hotel, Gornji Vakuf, and business premises and shops nearby were wrecked and looted." And, furthermore, it goes on to say: "To the commander of the Ante Starcevic Brigade instructions were issued to speak with Mr. Agic and try to calm the situation down and separate the conflicting parties and that they should undertake active defence," and that's been underlined, active defence there. "We're also following the situation -- developments in Bugojno where there are no clashes for the moment or any serious tensions." And it says: "The command of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina told the HVO that no motor vehicles must be allowed passage in the Gornji Vakuf area without previously gaining permission from them. Now, what is correct in that report and what is not? Could you tell us, please, just briefly, not to take up too much time?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: None of that is correct. At the time, Siljeg with his units that he brought in pursuant to an order of the 12th of January, he continued to shell and attack the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Fine. That is your testimony. May we have the next document, please, which is P 01110. It is a letter from General Arif Pasalic to the command of the 3rd Corps to be handed over by hand, Enver Hasanovic, to Enver Hasanovic personally, and it says: "Pursuant to an order from President Izetbegovic," and it is handwritten under 1: "A military political commission is to be established immediately with two representatives of the ABiH and SDA party at the highest level and send it to Gornji Vakuf. "2. Colonel Siljeg and Andric, representatives of the HVO, are to be contacted in Gornji Vakuf. Send me detailed information on the situation in Gornji Vakuf." And "4: Do have the patience while the situation in Gornji Vakuf is calming down." So that was an attempt made from the 4th Corps to do this together with the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Commission had its first meeting on the 14th of November.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I'm going to read you another document and then I'll be asking you some questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, just a short question. Could you clarify something. The document that General Praljak has just shown you from Pasalic to the 4th Corps to Hadzihasanovic who is the commander of the 3rd Corps, and under 3 Pasalic asks him to send him detailed information on the situation in Gornji Vakuf. Now, how come General Pasalic intervened here, intervened with the 3rd Corps? Have you got an explanation to give us? How was he able to do that and why would he do that. Because usually the corps were on an equal standing, and if somebody wanted to ask for a report from Hadzihasanovic it would have been the Supreme Command, not his colleague from the 4th Corps, for instance. So what explanation can you give us about that because we have the impression that the 3rd Corps is somehow depending on the 4th Corps and under the tutelage of the 4th Corps, if I can put it that way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in the preamble -- well, not the preamble but in the first line General Pasalic is referring to an order from President Izetbegovic, so I can only assume that in Jablanica he had a meeting with the president, and I think that President Izetbegovic was on his way to Geneva at that time. So in order to facilitate contacts, I think he issued this order to General Pasalic telling him to contact General Enver Hadzihasanovic and to propose these three points or four points. I have no other explanation. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me if I say that we quite simply were not able to establish cooperation and links with the 3rd Corps. Is that true, that we used the good relations we had with the 4th Corps who, let it be said in formal and legal terms at that time, was under the -- was subordinated in Mostar to the HVO, or resubordinated, and that meant nothing except that they should sit down and decide where they would go, which lines they would go to, and that Pasalic would ask for ammunition from the HVO. So because of those relations that we had with the 4th Corps and we did not have any relations like that with the 3rd Corps, Mr. Izetbegovic used this method to make use of these good relations and try to influence Hadzihasanovic to do the job as it should have been done?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly be asked to slow down for the benefit of one and all. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What do you think about what has just been said, Witness? According to what Mr. Praljak has said, there were difficulties with the 3rd Corps, contacts with the 3rd Corps, and so the HVO had to go through the 4th Corps in order to wield influence on the 3rd Corps. Would you say that that was correct, not correct? What is your opinion about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't see that there were any difficulties intentionally. Perhaps there were communication difficulties, but as far as I know General Hadzihasanovic had good cooperation at that time with the commander of the operative zone of Central Bosnia, that is to say General Blaskic. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Let's move on may I have P 01114, please, the next document. It is a collective piece of information with respect to developments in Gornji Vakuf, Mostar, and Travnik. We'll just look at the Gornji Vakuf paragraph. So may we zoom in on the Gornji Vakuf paragraph, see what that says. I have underlined the portions. It says from the commander of the BH army there's a ban on the movement of HVO vehicles without their permission. Because of knowledge about the possibility of large-scale conflicts which was confirmed on several occasions during yesterday; the day yesterday, there was gunfire at HVO positions in town and our units retaliated and -- towards the BH army positions in the evening hours and towards Gornji Vakuf. Colonel Siljeg set out for Gornji Vakuf with 200 soldiers and two tanks.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Might the English version be placed on the screens for the interpreters. Thank you. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Colonel Mandic Ilija had 50 soldiers. Colonel Andric was in Prozor, and during the day yesterday the members of the HVO and Bosnia-Herzegovina army were captured, about 15 members, who were exchanged later but without any identity cards, documents, materiel and technical equipment or vehicles. Yesterday afternoon five Ludvig Pavlovic Unit soldiers were captured by the BH army of course. Now, Brigadier --

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have a document 1141, and the contents of that document are different.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 0 -- P 01114, that should be the number of the document you should be looking at. 1114.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here: "Since the Christmas holidays Colonel Andric."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, yes, that's it. No, this is Akrips [as interpreted]. That's something different. In the middle. Do you see that it says that Colonel Siljeg set out with 200 soldiers and two tanks and that Predrag Mandic Ilija set out with 50 soldiers? You have that on your screen.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, why were the forces coming in at that time if you wished to calm the situation down?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, tell me this: What was the plan of attack to take Gornji Vakuf if it was only on the 13th that Siljeg arrived with 250 soldiers and two tanks? Were those sufficient forces? Was that a preparation for an offensive, a plan to take control of Gornji Vakuf with 250 soldiers and two tanks, or is his explanation that the conflicts had already begun, that they were gaining in intensity, and as a responsible commander he was bringing in half a battalion roughly and two tanks because he did not know what the intentions were of the opposite side or, rather, of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Vakuf, especially because the problems had reached a peak, and we'll see later on that there was trench digging and so on and so forth. So he comes in with 250 soldiers. That's what it says here. And with 250 soldiers on the 13th you cannot - and the conflicts had already begun - launch something which would be considered an attack to take control of the town. Do you agree with me there on a military level?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not agree with you there, General, because Colonel Siljeg up until that time in town had more than a thousand soldiers who were not from that area, and we know that just prior to the new year or, rather, after the new year a lot of soldiers arrived in Gornji Vakuf. Colonel Siljeg, on the 11th, was informed of the situation in Gornji Vakuf in order to write that on the 12th of January the town should -- control of the town should be established.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll come back to that order, and it was wrongly translated and as you can see Judge Antonetti noted that. The units were placed on the alert, but whether they would have gone ahead it says there no, not until the order was given, and I think that is quite clear to you as a soldier, and I'll try and explain it further to you. All the plans and all the orders were compiled after D-Day in Normandy and then they waited for the date when General Eisenhower with the united forces would see that the order be given and carried out. That is the military explanation and I'm sure you can agree with me there.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I can agree with that explanation. However, the order given by Colonel Siljeg was being applied as of the early morning hours of the 12th of January, and he didn't hide that from UNPROFOR. He came to the UNPROFOR base on that day. In the evening we did everything we could to stop this on the 12th of January. I said that we visited the lower villages where it was claimed that the problem was that the communications were made more difficult, but there was fear on -- only on the Bosniak side at that time, and I state that with full responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to ask you a question yesterday but we didn't have time for that. You were speaking of the UNPROFOR force in Gornji Vakuf. There was BritBat. Now, you yourself, as commander of the municipal Chief of Staff, did you have any relations with the commander of UNPROFOR, the UNPROFOR force in Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And who did you meet, as far as you can remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I met with the commander of the UNPROFOR base, Major Johnson, and on several other occasions I met with Colonel Stewart. On -- he came to the base for the first time on the 13th in the evening because his soldier had been killed at a crossroads.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And during these meetings with these various members of the BritBat, did you tell them orally that in your opinion the HVO was about to mobilise its forces in order to launch an attack against the BiH? Did you tell them that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They knew that better than I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You say they knew, but did you tell them as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That was the constant topic of discussion at UNPROFOR headquarters when we met. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Agic, I could agree with you that certain estimates in the ABiH reports may be incorrect because of fear, but Colonel Siljeg was an officer of the JNA, and not in a single document that has been shown, and I will show more of them, no mention is made of more soldiers. Do you think that in those reports, which are precise in military terms, that somebody would put 200 soldiers plus 50, whereas in fact there were 1.000? Is there a single document shown by the Prosecution or that you may show that the soldier known as the HVO stated somewhere which brigades these men came from, that they had sent 1.000 soldiers to Vakuf? Is there a single document, HVO document, to that effect? And these documents, at least in terms of numbers and dates, are correct because they were compiled by professional officers of the JNA. Siljeg may have been whatever you like, but when it comes to the compiling of reports, he was a major of the Yugoslav People's Army, an active-duty soldier, who wrote precise instructions all his life. So can we agree in that regard?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General, I don't know how Colonel Siljeg wrote his reports. I know how he spoke and how he behaved when we were sitting together and when all of us except him were trying to appease the situation. He used the language of threats. He didn't stop even on the day when the agreement was signed with the chairmanship of international factors. He threatened. He said that he had so much power that had they come 24 hours later there wouldn't have been any need to have a meeting. And this is -- the meaning is quite clear. As for these 250 soldiers on the 13th or 12th who came with him, he's simply reinforcing his troops for the attack. What did he need tanks for when we didn't have any tanks? A tank can only be used as a gun in Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Very well. We'll come back to these two tanks. It is his military right to do so, because in his opinion the conflict has started, and he believes that the other side is involved. But we'll come back to that. Let's not go into what he said there. I can ask you: Do you know that on the 18th in the evening I ordered a cessation of hostilities, and I stopped HVO units from entering Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why wasn't your order implemented in practice?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My order was implemented. You will see on the basis of the documents of the ABiH that HVO units at that point in time had the town almost ready. They could have easily entered the town. Do you know that on the 18th, following my order which was based on my authority, that all offensive activity of the HVO was stopped?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're talking about an order that you issued on the 18th. Do you have that order to show it to the witness? It's a written order or an oral order? If it is in writing, then you must have it. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Your Honours, witness will come. I didn't have it. I wasn't entitled to sign orders in those days. But on the 18th I issued an oral order, and I testified to that effect in court here four years ago. I called Geneva through Minister Gojko Susak, or Mate Boban, because General Petkovic, who was Chief of Staff, and he was there at the time, that they should immediately on the 19th send an official order on the cessation of military activities in Gornji Vakuf. That the 19th the HVO must go to attend negotiations and respect the cease-fire. Why it wasn't respected we'll see through the documents. I just hope I'll have time to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, you're telling us that you issued an oral order on the 18th following instructions that you had on the basis of the negotiations in Geneva. But if you issued an oral order, I don't know to whom. It must have been to Colonel Siljeg. Then he must have immediately passed on your order to his units. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mr. President, on the 18th I issued an order that they mustn't move, and after that I called to Geneva asking them to send a formal official order to Colonel Siljeg on behalf of General Petkovic or Mate Boban. So please don't misunderstand me. This order on my part was based on my influence and authority and not on the formal position I held at the time. There are some documents to corroborate this. Can we now move on? Let me show you a document now. The number is 19 3D 00487. 3D 00487. Do we have it?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have 486 but not 487. We need 487. Ah, it's reached me now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was issued on the 13th of January, and it says: "We also have reports that 13 members of HVO units were wounded in conflicts with the ABiH. During the day there was fierce -- a fierce conflict between HVO units and the ABiH. Croat houses were burnt in Luzani, and the same were expelled towards the positions held by our units." You saw this document yesterday. Is it true?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why didn't you say that on that day we had 15 dead, not to mention the number of civilians?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now another document, 3D 00476, please. This has already been admitted into evidence. 476. 3D 00476.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document has been shown to Their Honours. It has a large number of pages, and we will just note the following with respect to the kind of battles we had around Gornji Vakuf and whether the HVO was involved. Let me ask you three questions. Here we have a list of casualties, the dead and wounded, HVO soldiers in the conflict in Gornji Vakuf in the period from the 12th of January to the 24th of February, 1993. Now we have the list for each day, the 13th, the 14th, and so on. And you will see that on the 20th of January when the agreement was signed there were very high casualties. And when we add up the dead and wounded, that was our job to do that, 276 is the total number of -- 209 wounded, 46 killed soldiers, wounded civilians 7, and killed civilians 14. Do you see this list of the ITD sector of Ante Starcevic Brigade from Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do see it, General, but I would like to ask Their Honours if we could look at the list dated the 13th of January as evidence there were units coming from outside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These were units of the HVO who, on the 12th, as Siljeg said, came there. Those are the 250 men who came there. But my question is as follows, the first question: Such a large number of casualties in the fighting around Gornji Vakuf, was this due, (a), to the inability of the commanders and a lack of professionalism, were they badly trained; (b), was it because the conflicts were intensive; or was it, (c), because the fortifications of the ABiH on positions and main features around the town of Vakuf were exceptionally well-fortified and difficult to capture?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will give you my answer. It is true that you were attacking and that it is normal when someone is attacking to have very high losses. You were not in town. You had the highest losses. Half of the dead HVO soldiers were killed in town. You said a moment ago that on the 18th you captured the relay station. Please say now whether there was a single trench knee high there, but you presented it as if it was a concrete fortification. In fact, there was a repeater, a TV repeater there that was hit, and it fell apart after three direct shots. You know how you captured it under very heavy fighting. But those are facilities, Your Honours, which are 50 metres behind the buildings in Gornja Mahala in town. Outside that area, towards Pidris, we didn't have a single soldier further away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, the figure given by General Praljak has where been discussed with other witnesses. Can you hear me? Let me check. Are you hearing me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Through the documents which appear to be truthful that there were 40 killed, 207 wounded, plus civilians, if we proceed from the hypothesis that the HVO was attacking, they are attacking by shelling first. In all military manuals, we don't start with artillery fire -- with infantry fire. First comes artillery fire and later comes the clearing with the infantry. How is it possible that in spite of the shelling there were so many dead on the HVO side? You have just given an explanation that half were killed in town. Was there chest-to-chest fighting in the town itself, and if there were losses on the HVO side that means that you were numerous, too, and that you were able to respond to that kind of an attack. Could you give us some more details regarding the HVO losses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the HVO was trying to gain control of the town. It amassed its elite forces in town to take control of the centre of the town where the military police was. During the first few days the fighting was so fierce that the killed and wounded were lying in the streets. The eight nitroglycerine rifles that General Praljak ordered to be brought to Gornji Vakuf should have been new weapons which were meant to help them capture the town because there was no other way. So that materiel was regrouped as well. I have to tell you that a tank was brought into the middle of town too. The police building was targeted from a distance of 50 metres and directly hit. However, it is not easy to capture a town. As for the artillery you mention, Colonel Siljeg acted as proper soldiers. He started with artillery, very -- a very fierce artillery attack, but he didn't look at the results of his hits. When they gained control of Krstic, they killed 26 soldiers there. Not a single soldier -- one soldier survived under the dead, and it was only when they were piled on the truck that it was noticed that he was alive. Those trenches were captured with tanks, anti-personnel carriers. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are now mentioning trenches, and you say that at the relay station at Krc you will show us this place on the map. If there are not shelters, and believe me that I did tour that fortification line and I will have it filmed, it was so well fortified at Krc and elsewhere. These are hills which are 50 metres away from the town as the crow flies. The first question: Why did you dig such big trenches a month before?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not true. You should have told Their Honours there were trenches, but you should have said that Gornji Vakuf was reattacked in the summer of 1993, and that is when those trenches were dug.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is what I want to hear. Colonel Siljeg and Andric, and as testified by a British officer, and while I was there I insisted on not digging trenches between -- behind the backs of the soldiers. The enemy is at Radusa. No army will tolerate trenches being built on the hills around town. Another question: If the tanks reach the relay station, and they did, could they hit house by house and destroy the Muslim part of Gornji Vakuf, which is 70 per cent of the town? Wherever you fire from with a cannon you can hit these with precision. Why wasn't that done?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Praljak needs to explain to the Court why Colonel Siljeg, in the afternoon of the 19th, brought in addition to a tank a lorry full of explosives and fuel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to intervene here. The witness is asking questions himself instead of answering the questions he's been asked, which is what he ought to be doing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The tank had come to target Vrse. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, why would this be, as you say, at a distance of 50 metres from the houses in the Muslim district? If somebody wishes to do this -- let me ask you this: You know what an open town means in the military sense. According to your reports that we have here, Vakuf was about to fall. First of all I asked you whether you knew who stopped the attack. Now, in the military sense we should have -- you should have been called and said let's get the civilians away. Don't hide behind civilians or surrender. Now in that -- as MacArthur did in Manila. There is the responsibility of the commander to hand over the town and to proclaim the town an open town. This was not done because -- or, rather, I'm asking you why wasn't that done, if it was the intention of the HVO to take control of Gornji Vakuf, if that was a plan? Now which commander, when he has Karamustafic, when he has Bokletera [phoen], when he has taken control of positions above town which had been fortified in previous months, he has the HVO behind, in the rear, which commander, if he had the intention of taking control of the town, would not have made use of this? Either he didn't have the intention or he was an idiot. What is it, of the two?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's a very broad question. You have asked me -- put different theses to me. The tank was put there to target Vrse for one reason. Because of the depression, it was not able to target them, because of the houses were down below underneath the hill, and he was targeting the lines and trenches behind the back. He was dangerous. He was appointed by the commander of the armoured mechanised units, General.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, you say that in Vrse there were trenches that were being dug. We're not going to wait to go into battle in an open space, are we?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Very well. I'd just like to convince you --

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General, you're asking me why were the trenches dug. I'll try and explain this to the Trial Chamber. The HVO at Makljen always had company-strength forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I understand --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, Mr. Praljak. General, General Praljak said that before the 19th of January fortified Gornji Vakuf by digging trenches. Now I understood it that your answer to that was that that was done in June, not in January. So my question is a simple one. In January, before the 19th, that is, did the BiH fortify Gornji Vakuf by digging trenches on the hills, in town, or wherever?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, up until the 12th of January, not a single trench was dug, trenches dug facing the HVO forces or any other side because there was no need for that, and that is why we lost. In one day of fighting, we lost the relay station, and they came to -- right up to the edge of town. Isn't that right, Mr. General? Isn't that right, General? THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but Mr. Agic, I'm going to give instructions to dig those trenches and I'll photograph them. They were fortifications of the first order.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in July they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In July and January. And who dug them in after that?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Take a look at the UNPROFOR reports.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly ask to slow down, make pauses between question and answer and not overlap. Thank you. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One of the main points of the agreement on a truce which was signed is this: To withdraw the forces and to fill in the trenches, to fill in the trenches. I'm not going to go back to that question. May I have 3D 00368 as the next document now, please. It is an order of the 15th of January once again. Once again, it is Colonel Siljeg issuing an order. It says: "To accept the PGZ." It's a mobile group for setting up obstacles, about 10 people, and engage it to block the road from the village of Voljevac, and they are subordinated to the Rama Brigade commander. Number 2, one platoon from the Rama Brigade is to be directed as security to the village of Mackov if it hasn't already been directed there. One platoon from the Rama Brigade should be sent to the village of Dobrosin to secure the town of Dobrosin and Voljevac 6 if it has not been sent there yet. 4, to eliminate the forces of the BH army in summerhouses in the region of feature 1303 on the Crni Vrh by artillery fire. So according to that report, a group is sent to set up obstacles and block the road and then it also says that the forces of the BH army at that point in time were at Makljen, Crni Vrh, et cetera. Up at Crni Vrh. Now, at that point in time, on the 12th of January, that is the date we're talking about, did the units of the BH army on the 12th, 13th, and 14th, were they at Crni Vrh at Makljen?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Crni Vrh and Makljen are not the same thing. We were never at Makljen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Crni Vrh?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you know where this elevation 1303 is, feature 1303? It is the first feature after village of Boljkovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll show that on the map later on. But may I have the next document, P 01152, please. Forces are not sense to town in any of these [indiscernible]. This is done to deblock the town?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But this is what I'm saying. In the document, document P 00152, in paragraph C, and the document is once again signed by Siljeg, I believe -- no. It is signed by Milivoj Petkovic, although I think it's Siljeg's report to the Main Staff. And it says how much ammunition must be ensured for the HVO Brigade in Gornji Vakuf. The Ante Starcevic Brigade, 5 boxes, 3 shells, 60-millimetre ones, and 300 shells of 82 millimetres, et cetera, which means that this should be provided. But the 15 cases of ammunition and the 600 shells, mortar shells, 300 of one and 300 of another, 60 millimetres especially, which are anti-infantry, which is something that could be used against the town. Is that something we would use against a town?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you asking me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it would be reinforcement depending on which unit it was going to. I would like to -- I would rather comment on the paragraph referring to the enemy where it says that there is concern because part of the military police has gone on assignment to Gornji Vakuf. And it says the Petar Kresimir IV Brigade. What brigade is that?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's not important.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if it's not a secret could you tell me, please, then?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not a secret, no. It is Livno.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, right, policemen from Livno to come to Gornji Vakuf if we wish to calm the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have to intervene once again. My client would like to conduct a calm interview with the witness but it is a fact that he's not answering questions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, P 00141 is the next document I'd like to have shown, please. P 01141. And it is Mile Curcic who signed it, the chief. The date is the 15th of January, 1993, at 1130 hours, informing the Main Staff and so on and so forth. He says the night and morning passed relatively quietly, this is after a truce, with just sporadic fire, et cetera, et cetera. And he goes on to say: "This morning Colonel Siljeg issued the order to block the Voljevac-Dobrosin road so that the PZG can arrive to reinforce Makljen and Dobrosin and not to use the artillery in built-up areas without special permission, and outside built-up areas not to allow any movements of the BH army towards Gornji Vakuf, or to take up positions facing our forces." So that's what it says. This morning -- "Early this morning infantry fighting began again with the use of cannons by the ABiH army. There was a regrouping of forces," et cetera, et cetera. Forces were introduced from Konjic and Bugojno, fresh forces. And then it says: Certain facilities in the town of Gornji Vakuf and Bistrica, Luzine, and Hrvatske. Says: "We were not able to put out the fires and these facilities are on fire, are aflame." I asked you that yesterday. You said that according to you nothing was on fire. There was nothing burning. Now, 32, 33, 34. Is any of this correct here, what it says?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. This is what General Siljeg ordered. Now, as far as the fact that on the 15th of January the army, the BH army, used artillery to fire, I don't know. That's not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move on now. Document -- and the next document, I have it here under number 33, but let me check the proper number. 3D 00439. And it's BH army documentation. This particular document that you're going to see on your screen was signed by the commander of the 3rd Corps, Enver Hadzihasanovic, and it is addressed to the 38th Brigade, the 312th Motorised Brigade, the 309th Mountain Brigade, and so on.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I be provided with that document, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is 3D 00493. 493, yes. 3D 00493. That's the document. I don't want to enumerate all the brigades. There are -- were 11 of them. Eleven brigades were informed through this order. On -- and it is the 16th of January, the date. "On the basis of information gave during the night and in the morning of the 17th, reinforcements from Kiseljak will be dispatched to the HVO, and I hereby issue the following order." Under 1, we'll skip 1 and move on to 2. "To prevent all attempts at carrying out manoeuvre of forces and bringing in reinforcements which were attacking Gornji Vakuf without our permission, engage in the following activities," blocking, et cetera. And then it says: "In case of an armed attack, in case of an armed attack by the HVO against our forces, we should launch a decisive attack to break up the HVO forces and militarily defeat them, seize their weapons and equipment and take control of the territory." And then it goes on to say: "Act according to orders issued thus far in that connection." So before this particular order, there were other orders in that connection. May we have your comments to that text?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order, and I think it is in order and it's properly written.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we have 174, P 00174 as the next document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, before you go on to look at the following document, this particular document, the one we have on our screens from the command of the 3rd Corps, I'm not getting the interpretation, how are we to interpret it in military terms? Is it an order which says prepare to retaliate in case of a attack, or may we consider this to be an order that is telling the 308th, 312th, 306th and your own brigade to attack? So what would your analysis be in military terms, solely in military terms? How do you understand the contents of that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The commander of the corps is ordering the units here to be on the alert and to be ready to engage. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, to launch an attack and to capture.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If they are themselves attacked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's stay in military terms, on a military level. It is a pity that we had -- did not have any military experts in court before you. But in military terms, purely military terms, when an army is attacking, are there any preparatory actions, any meetings held, a plan, a general plan of attack which is then concretised on the basis of documents establishing that on such and such a day at such and such an hour the attack started or is to start and so on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. There is a whole procedure that is put in place. It is called making a decision, setting out -- doing reconnaissance working and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, this procedure in your country at the time, in 1993, was this the result of the old rules and regulations governing the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not receiving the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me repeat my question. You've just said that there was procedure that was put in place, and my question is this: I would like to know whether that procedure was inherited from the rules and regulations that were in force during the ex-JNA period.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the BH army, yes, that's right. It did apply.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, if there was an ABiH attack, would you normally find documents which would relate to that procedure for attack? Would there be documents relating to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Procedure for attack must exist of the superior commander, and everything issued must be complied with. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I would like to turn the question and ask it a different way. You recognise this order from General Hadzihasanovic, do you? That's right, is it? That's what it is; do you agree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, it is. I agree. Although General Hadzihasanovic didn't sign it. This is not the general's signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Now, to the best of your recollections, the attack, when it took place, that the general is referring to in this order, did the attack take place or not? If it did take place, then the preparative steps that President Antonetti mentioned, were they put in place or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Hadzihasanovic -- rather, this order is addressed to all units within Central Bosnia. This is not an executive order. Units are placed in combat readiness and are told to respond if they are attacked. By this order, General Hadzihasanovic is endeavouring to prevent the manoeuvre of HVO forces which might possibly have reached Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the meantime, let me just read a part. "Forces of the King Tomislav Brigade: 135 cannon; 120-millimetre mortar, 20 pieces; VBRs 107, 36; 6 shells; VBR 107-millimetres, 12; 120-millimetre, 10," a total of 89 shells.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we check the numbers?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [No interpretation]. P 01162, dated the 16th of January, 1993. Not counting the T-55 tank from Makljen, Colonel Siljeg reports that he used a total of 89 shells for the whole municipality. Is that what it says here? And is this a minimum consumption of shells for the whole municipality? THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Can we place it on the ELMO, please. That is not the document. Can you put it on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five pieces with a cannon on Svilici. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement, you said a thousand shells, but you will agree that a professional officer could not speak erroneously about firing. He says that he used, for the whole municipality, 89 shells, not counting the 155 tank which is at Makljen. That is far from Gornji Vakuf. Is that what it says here?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He doesn't say that a single one fell on Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He says it was fired.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, not a single target was close to Vakuf. This was the targeting around. Why was the 130 cannon fired at the village of Svilici?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All I'm asking you is for you to testify.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not a correct report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's not correct; fine. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Let's have the next document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this document that you are producing in support of thesis, in the paragraph B, "Our Forces," I read the following sentence: "We are beginning intensive operations on the enemy and the regrouping of forces of the ABiH." This sentence can lead us to believe that, at 2000 hours, on the 16th of January, Colonel Siljeg is explaining that he's beginning an attack. General, do you see this sentence? How do you interpret it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this report, in this document, I can't find that sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The sentence comes after the small heading "Our Forces" and before the forces of the Kralj Tomislav Brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have document 1162 in front of me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. In your language, the words are "Danas smo poculi."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's not the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You don't have the right document. P 1162. Do you see the small (b), "nasse snage"? Will you read it, please, in your own language, the sentence beginning with the word "Danas."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Today we have started acting more intensively on all movements and regrouping of enemy forces (ABiH)."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What does that mean, in military terms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It means they intensified their attack, introduced additional forces. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Could Mr. Petkovic please make a comment? THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would refer to this sentence once again. "Today we have started to act more intensively on all movements," and this refers to the forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the regrouping of forces of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. This means, if linked with the previous order by Hadzihasanovic of the 16th, that some forces are being introduced to Gornji Vakuf. Now, please, Your Honour, will you look lower down, where it says that Crni Vrh has been captured, and then the next sentence: "Enemy forces" - I am addressing you, Mr. Agic - "Enemy forces who tried to make a breakthrough towards the positions of our forces were fiercely shot at and rejected. We had two dead from sniper fire, enemy sniper fire. Both are reconnaissance members from the Rama Brigade." I repeat that the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina is carrying out the manoeuvre and regrouping of forces, and this sentence that says that enemy forces tried to break through towards positions of our forces were fiercely repulsed. And I link this to the report of the 16th by Hadzihasanovic when he says, "Introduce more forces and carry out an attack." That would be my comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, you have just heard General Petkovic. He tells us, in military terms, that the ABiH was regrouping and carrying out movements. To your knowledge, in this area, on the 16th of January, were there movements by the ABiH? Were there regroupings and reinforcements? Because, according to General Petkovic, this is linked to the document that we just saw by General Hadzihasanovic, telling you to mobilise yourselves if you are attacked. What is written here, does it reflect the reality, or is it your view that it don't correspond to the reality on the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the order by General Hadzihasanovic was not in this part of the territory. It couldn't be respected in this part of the territory. I beg you to bear in mind. Svilici is nowhere close to the line. This is a village of ten houses. I don't know why it would be targeted if it is not for intimidation. Why would five 130-millimetre shells be fired at it? This is the most powerful cannon that we have. But we leave that to the person who fired these shells. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Can we move on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is now time for the break. The registrar tells me that you have already used 100 minutes, General. Do not forget that after you there are 35 minutes for Ms. Nozica and also 35 minutes for Ms. Tomic at the back. So please make your own calculations, because we have to adjourn at 7.00 p.m. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it's a pity that all the hundred documents prepared cannot be reviewed, because this is an ideal opportunity. I think I'll be able to finish in another 15 minutes. Have you given me some time?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think as we still have another one and a half hours until the next break and another hour from 6.00 to 7.00, if he uses another hour after the break I think the remaining two Defences will be able to complete their cross-examination in the time left, because we are all keen to hear what General Praljak has to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It is a quarter to 4.00. We will have a 20-minute break and resume at five past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resumed. I just have an announcement to make for the interpreters. They have noted that we're all speaking much too fast and that they find it very difficult to follow. So I myself will do my best and I hope all the rest of you will do, too, to speak slower to facilitate the work of the interpreters. Having said that, Mr. Praljak. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Next document, please, and it is number 3D 00531.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier Agic, would you look at your screen. It will come up on the screen. You needn't waste time looking through your folder. The number is, and I repeat, 3D 00531. And here it is. This came by Paket post, and it says Hadzihasanovic, the unit of the 4th Corps, deployment of the unit of the 4th Corps, and he proposes that it be sent out urgently, on the -- or, rather, that the unit numbering the rank of a brigade be urgently dispatched from Jablanica to the broader region of Makljen to launch an attack on HVO units in the area of Makljen. The axis for the bringing in of reinforcements and engagement of forces pursuant to a decision by the brigade commander and he proposes that it be the Neretvica Brigade. This is urgent. It says "this is urgent" at the bottom in handwriting, at the bottom of the document. Is this indeed a document which has the cryptoprotection, it's encoded, and was sent out to the following addresses. Now, is this a proper document? Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume it is. I assume it is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Next document, please. It is 3D 00531. 3D -- I repeat -- ah. It's 3D 00499. 3D 004, et cetera. It's rather faint. I have a better copy in my own hands. It says: "Contact Lendo Refik." He has been granted permission to provide artillery support. And the signature is that of Commander Enver Hadzihasanovic. Can you see that document?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see the date. I'm just interested in the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could this document be placed on the ELMO. The date is the 18th of January. To the 317th Brigade and Lendo. You know who Refik Lendo is, I assume? Or, rather, do you know who Refik Lendo is?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is Refik Lendo being asked to provide artillery support to the forces of the 317th? And was the okay given?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said that there was no artillery of this kind in Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. May I have document 3D 00498, please. Once again, it is a document signed by Enver Hadzihasanovic, the commander. And it says -- or, rather, he repeats that the Neretvica Brigade was asked to be dispatched to Makljen from the composition of the 4th Corps and that they would be informed -- receive timely information. And this is sent to the 307th Motorised Brigade in Bugojno. Now, why was Bugojno included in all this? We don't know at this point in time, but is that what this document says?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the document says, but I don't think that the signature is Enver's, but I do think that the document is authentic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Next document, please. My number is 47, but let me find the other number. It is 3D 00496. The date is the 18th of January. It is the command of the 3rd Corps. The year is 1993. It is signed by Commander Enver Hadzihasanovic, and once again addressed to the 307th Brigade in Bugojno. And it says as follows: "You did a good job in posing an ultimatum to the HVO, but take care and leave your large forces in Bugojno both because of the Chetniks and because of the HVO, and set aside as many troops as possible and advance to Gornji Vakuf. Also inform if you come across resistance from the HVO, enter into an all-out open conflict and tell us whether a sabotage reconnaissance detachment has been detached to Bojska and Grnica or whether it is stationed there, and if it has indeed set out, whether it has conjoined with the IG in the region of Jagnjid and Drazev Doca. This assignment must be carried -- it is compulsory to carry out this assignment." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because on the 18th of January Gornji Vakuf was almost taken control of, as was the territory around it. You didn't expect us to wait, did you?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I didn't expect you to wait, but I'm just going through the documents. And the next document now is P 01 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Slowly, slowly. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Document 3D 00452. The document is 3D 00452.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here, Mr. Arif Pasalic, the commander of the 4th Corps, is writing to headquarters and staff of the ABiH to Sefer Halilovic in person. And he says as follows: "On the 19th of January, 1993, along with the presence of the EC with Mr. Petkovic, the commander of the Main Staff, an agreement was reached and a proposal made for a cease-fire in Gornji Vakuf." First, the Main Staff of the HVO, Bruno Stojic, Petkovic Milivoj and Pasalic Arif would issue an order on the cessation of hostilities in Gornji Vakuf, and the order would be signed by the Main Staff HVO, Bruno Stojic and Arif Pasalic, pursuant to your authorisation which would apply to the conflicting parties. The representatives of the European Community would be the mediators in this regard with us. "To all units of the HVO and ABiH we would give assignments to reduce tension, and we would send commissions numbering six members, three from the HVO and three from the ABiH, to implement it and issue an order to deblock the roads. We would like to have your opinion urgently." Is this a valid, authentic document?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it coincides with the right date and the commission that signed the truce, the cease-fire, in Gornji Vakuf on the 21st of January.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you agree that intensive work was under way at that time to implement the cease-fire already on the 19th. May I now have the next document, please. It is my number 66. Otherwise, it is number 3D 00505. 3D 00505. 505. Page -- that's the second page. May we have the first page of that document, please. Page number 1, please. It is Mostar, the 24th of January, that is to say five days after the 19th. Once again, it is the 4th Corps command. The commander is the same, Mr. Arif Pasalic, and he is issuing the following order. Under 1: "Accept the unit DIO 004 into your own composition." But I'd like to dwell on paragraph -- or point 6. "During the fortification of the units, the battalion officer should contact the commander of the Prozor battalion, Mr. Ruvic Salih, in order to exchange intelligence information about the enemy and the territory." When it says "enemy" here, does that imply the HVO?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll see from point 7. "Send reconnaissance groups in order to carry out reconnaissance work along the axes at the Makljen feature where working with the local units they should see the lie of the land, the capacity of the axes, the deployment and numerical force of the HVO along those axes as well as at the Makljen feature itself. "8. After carrying detailed reconnaissance work, after evaluating this, issue precise assignments to the units in order to carry out active operations with the aim of inflicting losses on the enemy, taking over combat equipment and taking control of the Makljen feature in order to prevent fresh troops from coming in from Western Herzegovina to Gornji Vakuf. "The Makljen pass" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm sorry to interrupt you, General Praljak, but I would like to ask a question, also from the witness, because when you induced this order you mentioned that at that time, that is -- I believe it is 24th of January, there was no combat activity in that region. At the same time, in the chapeau, the preamble of this order, you can see that, that it says that -- "to provide support to the 3rd Corps, 317th Mountain Brigade, currently fighting the HVO in Gornji Vakuf." So I again repeat: "Currently fighting the HVO in Gornji Vakuf." Now, my question is: If it is put there in the chapeau that "currently fighting the HVO," I would like to ask the witness, Brigadier Agic, if it was indeed during that time fighting was going on or not, and then of course it should shed light to the question if there was any fighting activities around that region. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I said yesterday that a truce was signed on the 21st under the auspices of the international community. However, none of the points in the cease-fire agreement were adhered to and operations continued continuously. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'd just like to read out the document to the end to -- so that we can see why the truce wasn't respected. We can see that from the order, because Mr. Arif Pasalic on the 19th is asking for it, and the commission was sent on the 24th as well as the other documents on the sending of sabotage units, a show who did not wish to see this cease-fire come into force. I don't know why, but can we look at the next sentence. "The Makljen pass should be held and you should entrench on the same feature and, if possible, launch active operations with the aim of having our forces enter Prozor." So not only - although Makljen is at a distance from Vakuf, about 10 kilometres away - that they should reach Makljen and engage in active operations enabling our forces, that is to say the ABiH forces, entering Prozor. And it says: "This order comes into force immediately and must be carried out immediately. And the Neretvica Brigade commander shall be held responsible for that."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not questioning the clarity of the order. I'm only asking you whether you have any comments to make with respect to the document and the signature and so on.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see the signature. I don't have any reason to doubt its authenticity, but you were going to go back in November to Prozor and you didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I have the next document, please. It is my document 75, but otherwise document 3D 00371. 3D 00371 is the next document. 371. I apologise. It is 3D 00371. That's the document. Once again, it's the 28th of January, 1993, signed by Mr. Arif Pasalic, commander of the 4th Corps. And I'd just like to ask us to focus on the following. "In this connection," it says, "it is necessary to prevent all arms transport -- transports, mines, explosions for the purposes of the HVO." He is ordering that at all check-points controlled by the ABiH army and the military police that there should be a stepped-up control, a passage going that way, through the check-point. Equipment, materiel, soldiers, and so on. And that same person is ordering that all movement by HVO forces should also be prevented along with all the other things he mentions. Has that document been signed by Mr. Arif Pasalic?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is a document of the 4th Corps. You probably used the roads to transport materiel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you signed the cease-fire.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was, but you didn't abide by it. The army had to react. We couldn't just wait, sit and wait.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is your opinion. The HVO -- I'll ask you that at the end. But the HVO stopped in front of the town, as we have already said, but we will clear that up with the other witnesses. Now I could have another very important document, 3D 00501. Will you please listen to it carefully. It is issued on the 20th of January, 1993, the command of the 3rd Corps is sending to the Staff Command in Bugojno, the 317th -- I am sorry, the 307th Mountain Brigade, and it says, I'll read it slowly and carefully: "We appreciate your thoughts and suggestions, but we draw your attention to the need to carry out assignments in your zone of responsibility. Do not engage in activities which are not within your terms of reference. Write your reports in such a way that they reflect the combat situation rather than being political lectures. In the conflict in all towns -- for the conflicts in all towns of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, it is premature even though such an option has been envisaged. Do your best to do everything you can to assist Vakuf." So let me say this one again. As it is too early for conflicts in all the towns of Herceg-Bosna, even though such an option has also been envisaged. This is Zenica, the 20th of January, 1993, signed by Enver Hadzihasanovic, and stamped. Now, sir, tell me, please, who is it who is making political statements in the army, and what kind of an option is this, the option of attack and conflict in all towns of Herceg-Bosna which is still premature?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid you'll have to ask the author of this request. I just see corps commander. He didn't sign it. But it's authentic as it has the stamp of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One more document and then I'll be done with this part of my cross. Could we have now 3D 00500. 3D 00500. Colonel Zeljko Siljeg, an extraordinary report dated the 20th of January. "According to subsequently received report," he says, the first paragraph, "in Gornji Vakuf it has been more or less peaceful. This morning we started to break up enemy forces at Vrse. The enemy is continuing to make a breakthrough from the region of Luzani-Grnica towards Ricica, Hrasnica, and Bistrica which has been repulsed. However, according to a subsequently received report, yesterday 26 wounded have been brought to the hospital in Bugojno by 1400 hours, four from HVO units, 12 from ABiH, and 10 Muslim civilians. Because overcrowding in the hospital, they are requesting the evacuation of about 25 wounded. Sir, was it true that the HVO medical corps, without any reservations and without any exceptions, transported wounded of the HVO and of ABiH to the HVO hospital in Bugojno?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
