utterances.text: I say with responsibility that you did not transport a single wounded person with your means but the hospital was a joint hospital. This was formed by the ABiH and the HVO. You're justifying your attacks and exaggerating ours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I have the next document, 3D 00503. Dated the 23rd of January, signed by Enver Hadzihasanovic on the next page. He says in paragraph 2: "It is our view that there is a problem in the organisation." First page, please. Page 1, please. I'll refer to only two points. "It is our assessment that there's a problem in the organisation of the same, meaning the units of the ABiH, and their involvement in combat activities. It is necessary correctly to assess one's own forces, planned, use, order, and implement the idea to the end." Number 3: "By issuing an order to all units, carry out active combat activities, especially offensive ones." This is to the command of the 317th Mountain Brigade in Gornji Vakuf: "Active combat activities, especially offensive." This was issued on the 23rd of January, after all the cease-fires. In all the documents we have read, there's reference either to attacks or sabotage groups or the Neretvica Brigade at Makljen or the entry into Prozor or the like. Paragraph 5 refers to the correct handing over of ammunition. And on the last page it says -- can I have the last page? "We cannot send units the way you imagine and wish due to other circumstances which you are not aware of, and you will be told about them personally by Selmo Cikotic. Your assignment, I repeat, is with available and additional forces to urgently plan and organise defence and at the same time engage in active operations for which you have already received instructions." The post scriptum: "PS: From the 4th Corps of the ABiH the following have been sent to you in Gornji Vakuf: 120.000 7.62-millimetre bullets, 150 shells for an 82-millimetre mortar, 120 shells for -- I'm sorry, 150 mines for the 82-millimetre mortar, and 120 shells for the 120-millimetre mortar. And today," on the 23rd of January, 1993, "we have sent 50.000 rounds of 7.62 millimetre, 16 RPG shells, and 1 PAM." It is an anti-aircraft cannon of 23 millimetres, if I remember well. Is this a valid report?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a PAM. It's 12.7, not 14.5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, fine. I made a mistake. Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the document correct, valid, authentic?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is a valid document, but if I may comment on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. When did the mortars reach you and how?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have noticed from this document that the army was not ready for the beginning of the conflict in Gornji Vakuf. Everything that arrived was in response to a reaction of the 3rd Corps. You just a moment ago said that Vakuf was about to fall. Surely you didn't expect us to let you enter the town?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, but on the 19th a cease-fire was signed, and from all the documents that we have viewed up to now, Brigadier Agic --

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was signed on the 21st, not on the 19th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go slowly, all right? The cease-fire was signed on the 21st.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But on the 22nd you captured the last feature, Ali Pasa's hill, and you put us in a position of a total encirclement. You know that we couldn't send wounded to Bugojno without an UNPROFOR escort.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I can understand that, but then how did you receive this?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This reached Priboj Boljkovac and then you know it was very difficult to carry out these instructions. It took days for these -- for this equipment to reach us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: I add my voice to that of our president. At the beginning he emphasised that you should wait for each other to complete your statements, and after when the interpretation is being finished then you start again with your questions or with your answers. Please kindly defer to this procedure and not to speak so fast. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, I want a point of clarification. General Praljak, through a series of documents, is showing that the 3rd Corps is sending, in terms of logistics, mortars, artillery, et cetera. So there are documents showing that as of the 21st of January, weapons are being sent. However, you have just said that Gornji Vakuf was rounded, encircled, and my understand was that you were explaining that these dispatches could not reach you because you were encircled. Could you tell us whether during this period of time you were really encircled and that you received nothing from the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Some of the equipment reached us through mountain roads via the village of Vrse. When on the 22nd Ali Pasa's hill was taken, all communication was interrupted with the outside world.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So within Gornji Vakuf you did not have the mentioned reinforcement -- reinforcements in materiel.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nothing reached the town from what was sent by the 1st Corps. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here it says that shells arrived, not mortars, shells for mortars.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General, one cannot have 120-millimetre mortar. Where can I shoot at with it? It's impossible. You took the relay station, the Partisan cemetery. You were holding Zvizde, Grebine. The features that I have mentioned, it's so nearby that you can recognise people. It's about 150 metres as the crows fly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, Brigadier, that is the best evidence that you are presenting to show that the HVO being in such a position did not want to take control of Gornji Vakuf. Not a single soldier who was in such a position and who at the beginning of the story aimed at taking control of Gornji Vakuf would not have missed such a chance. You don't have to be a military expert to know that. From what you say -- tell me you don't agree. But from what you are telling us, it is quite clear, but you can say, "I don't agree," my question is: Is it clear from that, that -- the struggle, the combat started in a different way and that the aim of the HVO was to deblock the very poor position that it found itself in because of the trenches dug by the ABiH so that the HVO had to make another road? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you're not right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. 3D 00502, please. I have just two more documents and the map. I'll be through in a minute. That is the document. Again, it is dated the 21st of February, 1993. The command of the 3rd -- of the 4th Corps. It is the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the ABiH, state commission. Esad Ramic, you will agree, was a member of the state commission for the cease-fire between the HVO and the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There's a document showing that. We saw it yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he says: "The commission worked in two parts today. One part with European Community and UN observers or -- that is UNPROFOR. They went to Pajic Polje so as to discuss with local commanders of the ABiH and the HVO the assignments regarding the withdrawal of local units and the filling in of trenches, the filling in of positions. They were given a deadline for the completion of works, which was specified by a plan. The other part of the commission went to the broader region of the village of Bistrica to jointly check to make sure whether all the bunkers and shelters and trenches had been filled in and units withdrawn because the agreed deadline has passed." And furthermore regarding Mr. Pasalic -- for Mr. Pasalic. "Today at a meeting the deputy commander of the HVO Rama Brigade from Prozor complained that last night there was a fierce attack by the ABiH from the direction of the villages of Here, Scipe and others, and requested that UNPROFOR and the European Community and the mixed commission go there to that region. It is my view that the attack must be stopped and that the men you have sent there should" -- will you move the text up, please -- "should work on the organisation of the defence and strengthening the military organisation rather than attacking, because all operations in Gornji Vakuf have been halted. "Signed on behalf of the ABiH, a member of the commission, Esad Ramic." My question is: Is it clear from this that -- that it is a question of implementing the truce, bringing units to Makljen, sending sabotage units? And this is testified to by Esad Ramic, a member of the commission for the cease-fire. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about Prozor, whether this is true that on the 21st immediately after the cessation of hostilities in Gornji Vakuf, it is clear from the report from Bistrica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it say here that the most important thing is to fill in the bunkers and trenches?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Siljeg at the commission meeting said he will not fill them in. He will, rather, capture them. And that is when the problem arose. The next morning he attacked Ali Pasa's hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So you're saying that we have a situation with Gornji Vakuf being surrounded. The HVO has cannon, artillery, mortars, more than a thousand men coming from another region. You do not have any artillery inside. You do not have anyone else coming from the outside. You are surrounded. And just then the HVO demands a cease-fire. The cease-fire is being signed, and the offensive operations by the army continue. Is this visible from all the documents that have been shown? Is it as clear as clear can be?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You keep saying that I am not attacking you. Show me a single feature that the army attacked and captured in this period of time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Agic, I never claimed that HVO or army BiH attacking. My thesis is completely different. I will put it to you and you may agree with it or you may say it is not true. It follows as this: The fear that existed among army BiH after Prozor because of possible incidents caused trenches to be dug on all important elevations around the city of Vakuf. HVO insisted over one and a half months at the end of 1992 for such a position -- that if such a position was militarily untenable because HVO units and the part of the town, smaller part which was Croatian, were put in such a position that it was possible from your part to effect an attack at any time. For instance, there were two lines Releg Krci [phoen], and the one on Radusa, and for these reasons, for mutual fear, they engendered -- this fear engendered tensions. And the conflict grew step by step; first some shooting in the city, then unruly units on the part of the Croats, the so-called HOS, although it was not under the command of Tokic. On your part, Hanefija Prijic over which you had no command or control, who in 1993 killed three humanitarian workers from Italy. You had drunken people, cafes which were open, and the conflict grew spontaneously because of different options from the military point of view. You were afraid of the HVO. HVO was afraid of you digging trenches. There was no plan to this attack. I did not say that you attacked, but can you agree or you may say that my thesis is incorrect?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not comment. I will neither confirm or say otherwise. There's no need for that. I don't believe that anything happened by chance. Yesterday we read commands that you referred to that we were -- we had to become subordinated to the HVO in the Croatian provinces. It is true that a number of incidents intensified the situation and blame can be discussed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, this is my basic thesis. It is said in the report of the 3rd Corps about the ultimatum. Their express position of the HVO as they state, I can go back to document but I like the term, the filling in the trenches and the return of units which do not hail from that period to go home, and this is the only position. And when the cease-fire was signed, exactly that is stated in the cease-fire agreement. Units to be sent home and the trenches to be filled in. And we've heard that in testimony of several witnesses. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did that after the 14th of February with great difficulties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 3D 00542, my last document. 3D 00542. It is a handwritten memo signed by Mr. Jasmin Jaganjac. My question: Do you know who Jasmin Jaganjac was? Say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that at that point in time Mr. Jasmin Jaganjac was a military advisor to the President Alija Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the 12th of February, 1992, is the correct date, then this may not be so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is exactly what we're going to refer to. It is clear that this refers to 1993. From the content this is 1993. You will see from the content of the letter that it refers to events in 1993. Let me read it out to you. "During today's contacts with General Praljak and General Cermak, I agreed that a certain amount of equipment and materiel to be sent to Pazaric, and I specify: 300.000 rounds, 200 pieces for RPG, and 20 pieces of Maljutka. "Materiel is symbolic, but passage has been ensured." This was addressed from Zagreb to Mr. Alija Izetbegovic on that date in 1993, the 20th of February. "I gave to Mr. Praljak and Mr. Susak," Susak refers to the Minister of Defence of Croatia, "your proposal of a statement that you forwarded to Mr. Boban as a proposal." Could you please scroll down. "They believe that it's quite approximate, and they admitted that they have not studied it sufficiently. "In answering to my question whether they've given up HZ Herceg-Bosna, General Praljak said that this no longer existed and that there is a period of transition that will be necessary." I will skip a part. I believe that we got stuck on item 5, insignia. "Praljak believes that this will not be a problem for -- apart from the state flag of Bosnia-Herzegovina to have a provincial flag. If any dispute were to arise, I will inform you tomorrow. Since General Praljak is travelling to Herzegovina tomorrow and after that to Central Bosnia, he asked me to relay to you that he wishes you to appoint one or two highly regarded Muslim politicians who would together with him visit Central Bosnia and try to influence in the direction of further diffusion of tensions." Later on, we cannot read it out, the letter refers to some ploys and back-stabbing within the SDA and other political structures. Therefore, is it clear here that on the 12th of February while fighting is going on in Vakuf, I organised convoys of munitions for ABiH towards Pazaric? Is it stated so here in this letter? Does it state here?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is too serious to be written in longhand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it say so?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does say so here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I repeat my question? In this period, whether Mr. Jasmin Jaganjac was military advisor to President Alija Izetbegovic

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether he was an officer of the Croatian army or HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you questioning me?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know in April 1993, because there is photo of him, but I never saw him before that time with President Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Agic, we are both officers. Your task is not to ask me questions. I have the right to put questions to you. My question to you is whether you know that Mr. Jasmin Jaganjac was at that time personal military advisor to President Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether at that particular time he was personal military advisor to President Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it state here that Praljak and Susak state and ask him to relay to President Izetbegovic that by signing of the Vance-Owen Plan or any other plan to be agreed upon by the side that there would be a termination of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna? Does it state here?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I commented. I could have written this myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it state so?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in -- under item 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, under item 3. And the last exhibit concerning this, whether you know that Mr. Jasmin Jaganjac was a Croatian army officer.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard talk about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that we asked him that in his capacity of a Croatian army officer to take over the command of the HVO in the city of Mostar in May 1992? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that Mr. Jasmin Jaganjac is a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I have no reason to doubt that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, a Muslim, Jasmin Jaganjac, was brought to Mostar in May 1992 to become commander of the HVO. Do you know that or not?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that he was in HVO in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we see the map? It is an exhibit. You take a look at the map. It's 3D 00543. On the basis of all the reports that have been read out in this courtroom, be it from the HVO or the army BiH, 3rd Corps, 4th Corps, brigades, et cetera, et cetera, we prepared this map with a deployment of forces on the 12th of January, 1991, and it was later on amended, those serpentine forms, indicating where the Neretvica Brigade had to be deployed and where different sabotage groups had to be infiltrated in the rear all within the ranks of the HVO. Mr. Brigadier, would you take a look at this map.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this the state of affairs on the 12th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. So 12th of January, 1993. Blue lines denote the positions of the HVO, and green denotes the positions controlled by the army BiH, and arrows indicate the further developments, green and blue arrows. My question would be: Next to Gornji Vakuf, elevation 128, then Strmica 785, then the next elevation 785, in a row those above the main road. My question is whether you controlled these positions from June 1992 from well-fortified positions.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute, General, we have to be more precise here. General Praljak is showing us a map with the positions of the ABiH and of the HVO. Now, do you agree with these positions, or are you saying that they are not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I indicate two errors? This map is not true. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you indicate them?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, did you come to the Gornji Vakuf command headquarters? Please answer this question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Probably in 1992.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this period and the 15th or 20 -- 25th -- the 31st of January.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I came on the night of the 15th and 16th of January to put a stop to all this, but we will leave it be.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a document HVO states that army of BiH took control of the right bank of Vrbas at Batusa, then Branovaca [phoen] alongside the Vrbas River, and those alleged positions are parallel. I must tell you that this is the road that the HVO used and used to travel down to come command headquarters which was adjacent to the UNPROFOR, and they controlled this road all the time until the 4th of August, 1993. Below Batusa in the northern direction there was no members of the ABiH. They used this communication, this road, regularly, and we had to use APCs of the UN to get there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But this -- it states here -- I'm asking you about Karamustafic.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can start from here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Grebine, Zvizde, who controlled the elevations around the city?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zvizde was controlled by the HVO continuously. We never held that position, the ABiH. And you rolled barrels full of explosives from that position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Until the August of 1993 we did not control this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm looking at the map, the one that General Praljak has just produced, and he's showing the positions of both sides. We can see Gornji Vakuf and we can see Batusa. Now, according to General Praljak, the HVO was deployed along that area and the ABiH was between Gornji Vakuf and Batusa. They were also deployed. And to the rear at elevation 733, Zvizde, you were also there too. Now, is that true or is it false?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, outside of Sicaja towards to Gornji Vakuf, to Krup, Franjkovac, north of the Batusa area, there were no BH army members. They used the road to bring in supplies, and that's where the Ante Starcevic Brigade command was throughout. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're saying the right thing. You used the road from the Sicaja pump, because at Karamustafic everything was blocked. Now, there was a witness here and she testified under a pseudonym and stated -- she's from a village around that area. She said that they made a road of salvation. Now, this road of salvation went from Sicaja to the village of Podgradje.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This road of salvation is the synonym for something else that was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We had another road of salvation where 200.000 -- or thousands of people passed through. This is from Sicaja to Podgradje. Now, I'm asking you this: Why did the HVO on the basis of testimony from a lady Bosniak Muslim witness had to devise this road of salvation with allies like yourself? Why? And this is something that the witness said.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- you made the road -- or route through Uzricje after you had taken control of Uzricje and made a road for yourself, a path for yourself, so that you could communicate unimpededly. But I'm saying that the map does not reflect the situation as it was on the 12th of January or throughout January and February. The BiH army was never in Franjkovac. It was never north of Batusa. You used that route to go to the headquarters, to come and go, and that's where the headquarters worked throughout that time. That's where they were. And I say that with full responsibility. Zvizde is a feature to the right of the Vrbas, looking at it from Makljen, the Makljen direction, right by the settlement at Odvode and another part of town which I've forgotten what the name of was. Mr. President, the ABiH army was never there, which means that's map is not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I can assure you that the positions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute, please. I have another question. We had witnesses here -- and I'd like to clear this point up. Next to Gornji Vakuf there is the village of Dusa and [indiscernible]. General Praljak is saying that those two villages were, in a way, surrounded by ABiH troops, because we can see the green line right round this area. Now, is that true or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Uzricje was surrounded. There was no need to surround Dusina because there were no soldiers there. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Unfortunately, the witnesses who were here challenged that and said something quite different, but never mind. You said that you were the commander of the town. You said that expressly.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, General, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But how do you know who was in the villages and what the situation was like there?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's not thousands of square kilometres, this territory. It's much smaller.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you go with the 317th or did you move around or did you stick to the town?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know the situation in the villages because part of the people who survived came into town, and we had the problem of finding accommodation and taking care of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you tour the area with your own two feet?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never left town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I'm very sorry that we haven't got more time, but thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you, too. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] I'd like to thank the Bench as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before the next Defence team takes the floor, I have two corrections for the record. Perhaps we could put that right straight away or shall we leave it until the end of the day?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 3, line 16, you gave us the exhibit number 3D 00476 and then the number was repeated 476 where it should have said 3D 00475 and 3D 00476. That would be the correct record. The next thing I'd like to put right is on page 12, line 20. It says the 14th of November, and that was the statement from the witness. It should have read the 14th of January, and we can see that from the previous text where the witness says two days after that, and that was the 12th of January. So it follows that the correct date should be the 14th. I have another correction to the interpretation, but we can go into that tomorrow or, rather, next week. I won't take any of your time up with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as page 3, line 16 is concerned, it was 3D 00475. You're quite right. That was the right number. Next Defence team. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. The time allotted to us by the Court for the cross-examination we shall be sharing with my client. My client and I will be sharing that time. Cross-examination by Ms. Tomasegovic Tomic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, before I begin, I'd just like to tell you that you have the number of the documents on a slip by the side of the document, but you needn't refer to the folder yet. Tell me, please, sir -- and I'd like to follow on from what General Petkovic was discussing with you, and he asked you about plan B. You said that you had never heard of plan B because you were in charge of Gornji Vakuf, if I understood you correctly. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean what was mentioned in General Hadzihasanovic's order?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. Plan B, 1992, the month of September.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never ever saw any document like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, do you happen to remember whether in September 1992 the commander of the TO Staff in Prozor was Mr. Muharem Sabic?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, may we have on e-court document P 00430. You have it in front you. We see at the top, while we're waiting for the document, that it is the TO Staff. The date is the 1st of September, 1992. It's note a view clear copy, but I think you will agree that it is the 1st of September nonetheless. It is signed by Commander Muharem Sabic. The title of the document is the plan of defence for Prozor municipality, and I'd like to draw your attention to the last few paragraphs. I'm going to read them out slowly. And it says here: "The first option is plan Elif, which would be carried out in a coordinated action with HVO units, formations, in accordance with document Alfa. The second option is plan B, which would be carried out independently or in coordinated action with the TO units in neighbouring municipalities (Gornji Vakuf, Konjic, and Jablanica) in accordance with document Beta herewith attached." Now my question is as follows: In view of the first paragraph I read out and the time period that we're discussing here, at that time the HVO and the Territorial Defence or, rather, the BH army were allies, were they not? Is that right? Fighting a joint aggressor of the --

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this leads me to a logical conclusion. I mean, you'll tell me if I'm right. In view of the second paragraph, which considers the possibility of the HVO and the Territorial Defence not being allies anymore but adversaries, in view of the fact that they weren't included together. Have I understood that correctly? That seems to me to be logical.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time that I see this document. It was another area, so I don't know about that, and I don't know whether you'll believe me or not, but this is the first time that I'm hearing of these two plans.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But now that you've read these documents -- this document in front of you, would that be logical to you? If you say you don't know, we can move on.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't wish to comment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to have on e-court the following document and it is P 00687. You have it before you. And it is connected with the previous document. So I'd just like to ask you -- or, rather, to read out certain portions of the document. It is from the security and information service, the SIS, of the Croatian Defence Council compiled in Prozor on the 1st of November, 1992. It is a report on clashes between the HVO and the ABiH in the Prozor area. And I'm going to read out paragraph 3, which reads as follows: "Based on a large number of statements taken from detained ABiH members as well as documentation seized from the ABiH, we learn that a plan for the neutralisation of the HVO in certain areas and establishment of full ABiH command had been made and prepared in advance. ABiH TG-1, Tactical Group 1, had two plans, the Alfa plan by which the ABiH units would act in cooperation with the HVO units against the Serb forces, and the better plan by which only ABiH units would act" -- I think it says TG-1 there -- "in case of clashes with the internal enemy, and in this case we know who that enemy is. "According to a statement by Ekrem Ubijar, Official Note number 01-71/92, given on the occasion of a meeting with some ABiH unit commanders from neighbouring areas, the following information was provided. "Mustafa Here cautioned those present that there would be clashes between the HVO and ABiH units, and he issued tasks to them as well as the axes of operations. "In the Makljen area, in a place called Crni Vrh, there was already a small unit from Prozor which was supposed to be a reconnaissance unit and controlled the already existing HVO units in this part of Makljen. It would meet the OS BH units from Voljevac and Boljkovac and serve as their guide. The units of the village of Pridvorci were attacked at HVO point on Menjik ridge and take the village of Glibe. The members of the armed forces of BH of the villages of Here, Kute, and Scipe, should take control of the village of Jurici and ensure safe passage from these roads to Prozor -- along those reads to Prozor and a breakthrough to the village of Uzdol which is where the HVO forces were located. The members of the OSB Kranjcici and parts of the village of Donji Vasti should neutralise" -- now, this is illegible and we can only see a few letters, "Rasim Pilav, commander of a private unit, should enforce a blockade of the road in the lower part of the municipality towards Prozor, i.e., control the main road from Jablanica to Prozor and neutralise the Croatian part of Kranjcici village, while the other Muslim villages would serve as reinforcement to the town. "In this plan were included units from the rest of Gornji Vakuf, or more exactly the Green Beret units, under the command of a man called Paraga, the OS BH Konjic units, and the OS BH Jablanica units were also in this plan." I'm skipping two paragraphs and moving on to a paragraph starting with the words "units from the village -- from the direction of the village of Boljkovac and Voljevac." This is how it reads: "Units from the direction of the village of Boljkovac and Voljevac have partially been successful in carrying out their task, and in cooperation with the unit withdrawn from the front line they took control of part of the Makljen area and killed an HVO member in the area who was driving a tractor with firewood for the winter. They did this from an ambush from the rear. And they pushed back the considerably stronger HVO -- more numerical HVO forces from the area. A strong unit from the direction of the village of Pridvorci broke up the Menjik point held by the HVO, took control of the village of Glibe, where an HVO member lost his life, and two others were captured, and they set fire to this part of the village. "Units from the direction of the village of Here took control of the village of Jurici and set fire to some buildings followed by an unsuccessful attempt to breakthrough to the village of Uzdol." And now I'm just going to lead the last sentence which is the first sentence of the last paragraph, where it says as follows: "Rasim Pilav's private unit attempted a breakthrough in the direction of Kranjcici but failed." Now, why have I read out all this to you. Regardless of the fact that you told me earlier on that you did not know of any plans, Alfa and Beta, are any of these events or military operations or names I've read from this document familiar to you for that period?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd first of all like to take a look at plans Alfa and Beta, because when I say that I didn't see them nor was there any talk of this plan with the armed forces, I say that with full responsibility. But I do know of this event when Prozor was taken and when the first echelon of HVO units reached Menjik and the army responded. We -- I think this is common knowledge. We used Maljutkas to fire. We missed, and that's the truth of it. The army had an order to do that, and some of the forces withdrew from Prozor and we were told to take them in. But it doesn't say here that the town had been attacked anywhere. During this period, the 24th I went to Jablanica to attend a meeting on that day. Prozor was on fire that day. There was looting. People had been taken prisoner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Sir, if I need additional explanations I'll ask you. All I was interested in -- or, rather, I know that you have a lot to tell us, but this document doesn't cover the entire situation in Prozor either before the events or after the events. All that I was interested in was whether any of these events actually took place. Now, why they took place, why they happened and so on?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The unit in Pridvorje was involved in the conflict in Prozor. Otherwise, the rest of the developments of these events was not properly described.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. We'll move on, and this is my last area that I wish to ask you about and it is this: Among other things, there was mention, if you remember, of that special report by Mr. Cikotic where the Mujahedin are mentioned, to remind you of that. At the time you said in answer to a question from the Judge that you were not aware of these Mujahedin because in those days in Central Bosnia there were not a single -- there wasn't a single Mujahedin unit. You don't know which Mujahedin this refers to, and the El Mujahid unit was formed after that period. That is what you said.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is so more or less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were in the zone of responsibility of the 3rd Corps. Will you please -- you nodded your head when I asked you whether you were in the zone of responsibility of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we now have document P 01318. You have it in your bundle. You have it in Croatian and in English. The English first and then the Croatian.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it a military report?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, it is a military report of a brigade battalion for the 27th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, of the British Battalion, interpreter's correction. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you look at the second paragraph, please. As far as I know, Travnik is about 30 kilometres from Gornji Vakuf. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not 30. You asked me whether it was 30.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how far is it?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but it's much more. It is 32 kilometres to Donji Vakuf, and then if you had to go to Bugojno 18, Novi Travnik another 20, and then Travnik and Novi Travnik another 10 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So up to 50 kilometres. Would that be right? If I've added up correctly. Let us look at the second paragraph, now, which says: "Normally a reliable source has provided additional information on the 7th Muslim Brigade. He confirmed that this brigade is commanded from Zenica with battalions deployed within the area of the 3rd Corps. A battalion from the 7th Brigade is deployed on the front line in the Travnik area. Members of the battalion consider themselves Mujahedin in every sense. The majority of members are staunch practising Muslims recruited from the local area. Although this particular battalion was instructed by two Iranians, the source claims that the brigade has, at most, 100 to 150 foreign Mujahedin from Islamic countries." Tell me, are you familiar with this?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said that I said that there were no Mujahedin. I continue to claim this. In Rostov and in the Gornji Vakuf area there were never Mujahedin units. A platoon of soldiers in the Rostov hotel belonged to the 7th Muslim brigade. How they declared themselves I don't know, but they were part of the 7th Muslim Brigade. It was officially a brigade of the 3rd Corps of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is Rostov?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is between Bugojno and Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have no further questions. Cross-examination by the Accused Coric:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Brigadier, I am Valentin Coric, and I have some questions for you. I would start with the 23rd of October, 1992. Yesterday you spoke about that date when it was said that at the Karamustafic check-point a unit of the military police was stopped that was heading towards Central Bosnia or, rather, Jajce. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said yesterday that you had an order from a senior command not to allow this unit to pass to Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because of the conflict in Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will use the reports that have already been used here and some which will be used in future. I won't quote -- I will just quote from some of those documents. When on the 23rd, and I wish to remind you that on that day there was a conflict in Prozor, the military police reached the Karamustafic check-point, and the commander was immediately told that they couldn't pass. The order on passage was issued -- was it issued before the military police reached the check-point?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you tell me, was it a mixed check-point?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The check-point was manned exclusively by members of the BH army police.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not true. You must learn that the check-point was informed and that Tokic agreed that the unit shouldn't pass that evening, and I said that I had received orders from General Hadzihasanovic not to allow transports of -- and convoys of any kind to pass.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you pass through that check-point?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was disarmed at that check-point two days later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any logs there?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not logs, but four engineering hedgehogs as soldiers call them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were they made of?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were made of iron.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. I have quite a different report.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know, because I and Zrinko together formed that check-point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll come to that later. So there were tree-trunks, and behind them were only members of the military police of the BH army. That is something that we will see from the documents and that we have already seen. Let me move on. Talking about the military police in Gornji Vakuf, who was the commander of the military police at the time?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was Mico, Bandic Miro, and Slavan Kvestic [phoen], one of the two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about ABiH military police, not the HVO military police. Who was the commander of the military police of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the police of the 317th Brigade was, I think, Hadzijusufovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Hadzijusufovic. Let us move on. We are now moving on to January 1993. At the beginning of the month the atmosphere was tense between the HVO and the BH army; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the beginning of the month the first incidents occurred; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They continued through December but intensified in January.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about the incidents in January. For instance, the motel was blown up in Gornji Vakuf; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was based in the motel in Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The civilian police was put up there and the reserve police of the MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer is no, but I have documents showing that the Green Berets were put up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were no Green Berets in Gornji Vakuf. I don't have time, but we'll come back to that. Was Hanefija Piric, known as Paraga, in Gornji Vakuf at the time?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not Piric but Prijic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. That evening when the motel was blown up, which housed only ABiH forces, do you know that Paraga was in the motel that evening?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, but it was not only the army units. It -- the motel was under the control of the MUP of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am claiming that Paraga was there that evening, that he had a unit there. What was his relationship with the military police?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know we had some problems with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was not my question. What was his relationship with the military police of the BH army in Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a commander who was relieved of his duties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prijic Paraga.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a member of the military police that evening when this happened?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The documents will show otherwise, let us move on. After this blowing up of the motel, who carried out an investigation to establish what actually happened at the motel?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the investigation was conducted by the public security station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is what you believe? Is it -- was the military police of the HVO allowed to participate in the investigation? Do you know this or not? Was it allowed or not?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know when this explosion occurred how many people were wounded or killed as a result of the explosion?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am claiming that no one was killed or wounded.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That is an answer too. Let us move on. At the time you were one of the most responsible people in Gornji Vakuf. What happened in Gornji Vakuf after this explosion at the motel?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You must give me a date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's say what happened in the village of Bistrica? Do you remember that three Croat civilians were killed, massacred? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Will you please give me the date?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The beginning of January 1993. The first day after the motel it explosion.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have it in many documents. The day after the explosion.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please give me a time, a framework.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's my mistake that I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was before the 10th of January. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Fine. And then something of great significance occurred in my opinion. This is before the conflict. Brigadier, so three civilians were killed and massacred. And one day at a joint check-point, Pavlovica and Karamustafic, where at that point in time the military police of the ABiH army and the military police of the HVO were manning this check-point jointly, was it? Was that true?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Karamustafic, yes, but at Pavlovica, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So we'll talk only about Karamustafic. Members of the military police were captured and detained of the HVO by the ABiH in Gornji Vakuf. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now let me see if you remember the following that I'm going to ask you about. Do you remember that members of the HVO in connection with this - so that is the capture of the military police - detained several members of the BH army at the beginning of January 1993? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am really sorry that I'm unable to answer, because you are not giving me a time frame.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All this happened within a period of five days.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were so many events in those days. I really can't remember half of those things that you are referring to, minor or major events. These events followed one another at great speed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I was in another state when this happened, but you were on the spot and you are not aware of it. But never mind, I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could there be pauses between questions and answers, please. THE ACCUSED CORIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I won't let you give speeches here. Their Honours have given me a fixed amount of time. I'm trying to throw light on certain events that are important. What happened was that the HVO detained several members of the BH army. After the first incident, do you remember that these members of the ABiH army were arrested and detained?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember either events.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you don't remember the exchange either?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. The police -- I was not always aware of what the police were doing. They belonged to the 317th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In those days in Gornji Vakuf there was the MUP of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The military police of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The military police of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The civilian police of 150 men attached to the republic's MUP. Did they have their own unit?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It didn't have so many men, but they didn't have so many men of the republic MUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there were two Military Intelligence Services. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know what happened on this side, but it was roughly the same on the other side too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that there were check-points set up by military units in Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That also existed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that it is the duty of the police to put up check-points in town or in villages?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If they had reason to do so, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will read from a document that has been shown here, so will you just confirm or deny this. I'm going back to the month of October 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Coric, we must have the break now because we have been working for more than an hour and a half, and we will resume at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resumed. Mr. Coric. THE ACCUSED CORIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Brigadier, I'm going to read out to you a short excerpt from a document P 00712. You don't have to follow it on the screen. I'm going to read out the salient part. I quote: "On the 24th of October, all units of ABiH are put into a combat readiness at 0500 hours. They take positions around the city." Gornji Vakuf is what is meant. "The trunk road through Gornji Vakuf at the place of Karamustafic is blockaded as well as all other local roads. Around 1800 hours an explosive device is thrown into a cafe owned by a person of Croat ethnicity in the part of the city controlled by the members of the ABiH, and after that armed conflict ensued. Street fighting lasted for around one hour when commander of -- Chief of Staff of the ABiH, Mr. Tokic, prohibited members of the HVO to open fire. After street fighting, members of the HVO take control of all factories and put them under their control." Brigadier, do you remember these events?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do remember these events. But the explosive device was not thrown in my earlier -- this was the cafe of Mr. Kovacevic, aka Ota, but it wasn't opened. And with respect to the facilities, they were divided. I don't know what could have been struggled over and captured.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm going to continue, and I will touch upon what I deem to be the most important problem in Gornji Vakuf. Incidents followed day in and day out. You said that half an hour ago.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In my opinion, you do not remember Mr. Paraga sufficiently. By this I mean Prijic. It says here Piric. I'm going to quote from three or two documents referring to that person. These are court documents. The first document, and I'm going to refer to their number, and I'm going to give you very short quotes. So document or excerpt from P 00952, says "Gornji Vakuf." "In the municipality of Gornji Vakuf there were no problems before the position of the military police commander of the HBH [as interpreted] before Mr. Piric, aka Paraga, was made commander. By his -- when he approached check-point at Pavlovica, Croats were disarmed, side weapons, vehicles, and other effects, personal effects. And mostly no receipts are given for such items which are seized. "Three vehicles from Prozor were also seized which were at the time in Gornji Vakuf. And to -- in order not to let this happen and continue from HVO military police from Gornji Vakuf made sure to disarm members of the ABiH which -- for which they did not have any licence to carry arms." This is what it meant. "But receipts are issued to such persons about personal effects or weapons seized. The Karamustafic check-point on the road between Gornji Vakuf and Prozor is operational only in day-time, and around 2000 hours both police forces would withdraw from that check-point." And you're going to be advised subsequently. And this was the report sent to me by heads of military police in the relevant time. Was the atmosphere like this as depicted in Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We had problems with the functioning of this check-point, Zrinko and I as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'm going to quote from another document which refers to Mr. Paraga but also sheds light on another matter. It's 2D 0023. This is a report from a meeting of ECMMs, ABiH, and HVO. The report says: "One of the representatives of the European Community stated publicly that all new problems are created by the army of BiH. He was embittered because planned visits of the Voljica village, Jagnjik, and Osrijedak could not be visited in a planned manner, and this was pre-empted by Paraga who said that the trenches would not be filled in, that there would be no peace or cease-fire before six people of his were released." Do you remember this event concerning the power of Mr. Paraga who could prevent people from UNPROFOR, ECMM, ABiH, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These trenches were filled in eventually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I did not ask you about the filling in of the trenches.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The answer eluded the interpreter because there's plenty of overlap, Your Honours. THE ACCUSED CORIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a report by a member of the ECMM at Gornji Vakuf. I'm not going to refer to his name. He said that he was a witness at a meeting and that the commander of the ABiH was familiar with him, and it was 31st of May, 1993, and he said that the same person, Paraga, he intercepted humanitarians from Italy, five persons, beyond Paljevica, in the woods, out of whom three were killed by his subordinates on the spot and two survivors reached the negotiations. Do you remember this event?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, because the brigade military police accepted the survivors. They conducted the investigation, and they -- and this Paraga was sentenced to 15 years in prison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to give you a [indiscernible], Mr. Bandic. What is his present occupation?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He works in the department J in the Joint Chiefs of Staff of the army of BiH. He is a security and intelligence officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. He was -- he was in the HVO throughout the conflict; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the conflict, yes, I believe so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know that there was some 50 members of the military police of the HVO. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the same time when Paraga was a member, and the others, they were contemporaries of Miro Bandic, military police of the ABiH had 150 members?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a company -- that's incorrect. There was a company, 120 to 125 men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm talking about police forces. Reserve MUP numbered 150; is that correct? I'm quoting from documents.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that they had reserve force, but I don't believe that this was the number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I did not invent that. I'm referring to a document. So you don't -- you're not sure?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Coric, your time is up. Otherwise, Counsel Nozica won't have her 35 minutes. THE ACCUSED CORIC: [Interpretation] Madam Nozica told me that I may proceed for another eight minutes. Is this true? So I've got, by your leave, another eight minutes. I was given that time by Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Paraga at the time would have command over some 300 people, reserve, his men and military police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where does Paraga hail from?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the village of Jagnjik, municipality of Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his occupation before the war, is Paraga's?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he was employed at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he was a freelance artist, then. Who was commander of Paraga while he was commander of the military police in Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Commander of the brigade, and he removed him from this position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when, but after the events that were connected with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When Selmo Cikotic was in Gornji Vakuf, who did Paraga respond to?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm -- with full responsibility, it wasn't Paraga.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then I have to resort back to my question who commanded the ABiH in Gornji Vakuf. So a couple of concrete questions: Where did you in the command of the 3rd Corps while Selmo Cikotic was in Gornji Vakuf; whether you sent daily reports to the HQ of the 3rd Corps? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. Did I send the reports through Selmo?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, you didn't get me. Concentrate, please. While Selmo Cikotic was in Gornji Vakuf, we couldn't ascertain which position he held. You said he was a coordinator. You were the commander of the defence of the town itself. So at that time, did you send daily reports to the 3rd Corps in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Every day. Did the commander of the brigades which covered the rest of the municipality send reports to the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the commander of the Jajacka [phoen] brigade or battalion at that time, did he send reports there?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then on the basis of which reports would Selmo Cikotic send his daily reports?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a member of the commission on the basis of his -- what he learned to the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was this?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in the Gornji Vakuf UNPROFOR HQ or base. He was every day there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wasn't he employed?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was there every day. He almost slept in Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I could not send any reports that you would send from -- from that period. I found Selmo Cikotic's reports but not yours, which means that Selmo Cikotic sent reports on behalf of all of you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Now the French translation is over, I would like to say the following: That yesterday afternoon when the question of the -- of the pecking order came up, that is who was number one and two and three in the chain of command, then of course we have discussed this question quite -- right away. At that time I found a document but right now I do not remember its number, which recalls a situation when there was a negotiation convened by the UNPROFOR and with the participation of -- of also the ECMM and the both sides from HVO and of course BH, et cetera, armija. In that list it was clearly stated that on behalf of the armija there were three persons there, and the number one listed was actually Brigadier Agic, and number two was Cikotic, and number three now I do not remember actually, but he was somebody from -- from their part. And of course there are the names also for HVO and also the UN people, et cetera. So therefore, I would suggest really to -- to close the issue that who was in command in Gornji Vakuf, because at least, according to this UN document, it was Brigadier Agic who was in command. But I do not want to take your time, Mr. Coric, so please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment. There's another question from the Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I'd like to go back for a moment to a problem that the accused Mr. Coric raised before the break, so I'm sure you'll remember that, and it had to do with the prisoner exchange. Could you tell us, please, if on the 12th of January, and also the 13th, 14th, or any of those dates, and I'm talking about 1993, of course, whether there were any Muslims captured by the HVO and whether there were any HVO soldiers captured by the ABiH and what the fate of those individuals was. Were they exchanged? Were these prisoners exchanged or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the standard practice on a daily basis was that at the check-points, both check-points, persons would be detained. They would be looted. Part of their property or their property would be seized. That was done by both sides. Now, in order to prevent the worst from happening and persons disappearing, the police was very effective, and they enabled these individuals to continue along the road they had taken by exchanging them, which means that the people who happened to find themselves at check-points, if their property had been seized, and if they reacted quickly enough, people were released straight away, and they were able to continue along their way. So this wasn't the classical type of capture. It was just that people were detained and mistreated. But the police was very efficient. And I said that this happened on a daily basis, so I don't remember that actual event. Because these were things that happened every day at one check-point or another. People were prevented from continuing along their route for a certain amount of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the soldiers under your command who manned these check-points, did they loot and seize property from persons and, if so, did you take any steps to sanction this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it wasn't the policemen that seized property. The policemen did their job. I'm talking about those people at the check-points who were individuals, individuals who did this kind of thing, but they did this for purposes of looting. Most of these individuals were apprehended on both sides.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So these check-points were not under your authority. They were individuals who set up their own check-points on a spontaneous basis in order to engage in looting along the main roads.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Coric, try and bring your questioning to an end because otherwise Counsel Nozica won't be able to do her job. THE ACCUSED CORIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. And I thank the witness for his answers. I have finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Counsel Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, and thank you for being careful and mindful of my time.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Agic, I'm sure that you, too, are quite tired by now, but we'll get through this very quickly. I haven't got many questions to ask you. Judge Antonetti just asked you something about these check-points, and it's a very important point, and would you agree that the reason that you gave in your testimony for some conflicts, or incidents shall we say, that took place before January 1993, and in that light, may we take a look at a document that the Prosecution -- that the Prosecution showed you. It is document P 00643, and it is an order. I haven't prepared these documents. I haven't got many documents, but you will see it come up on the screen. It is a short order signed by the commander Colonel Zeljko Siljeg on the 24th of October. Here it is on our screens. 1992 is the year. And the Prosecutor asked you to focus on the order for action, the title of this document. And the first paragraph it says: "Place the town under your control. Control the roads and be resolute in eliminating all attacks on HVO units." Now, let us look at the second paragraph of that order. "Maintain contact with the HVO Eugen Kvaternik Brigade in Bugojno and the Rama HVO Brigade in Prozor. Communicate amongst yourselves and, if possible, jointly liberate the communication line between Vakuf and Prozor." Does it not seem to you to be logical if this road was not blocked why, then, would this order have been written and asked that this main road, this main communication line leading from Bugojno to Vakuf be freed?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how you mean "blocked," how was it blocked.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I am indicating the verb "osloboditi" meaning to liberate. Does that not mean -- does that indicate that the road was blocked? Why else would you have to liberate it, free it?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, I'm not surprised by your answer, but I just wanted to draw your attention to this portion of the document which will be important when the Judges come to weigh up your answers. We have another document -- or, rather, this document is the 24th of October, right?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the fall of Prozor.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: But before the fall of Jajce, right?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yesterday you saw a piece of information compiled by Ante Prkacin, and for the record I would like to say that it is document 3D 00484, which talks about endeavours to reach Jajce by the HVO, because Jajce was in a very difficult situation at the time. Now, let's us take a look at P 00670 together.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it a report?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The number of the document is P 00670.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm asking you, is it a report.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It is not a report, no. In fact, it is the report you saw yesterday. It's rather illegible. The date is blurred, although I'd say that it was the 29th. But anyway, you have what it says in writing in the upper right-hand corner, and there it clearly states the 29th of October, 1992, and we're talking about those roads, those communication lines. So let's see what it is that you do not -- what it is that this has created, and you say you don't agree with it. It says: "We have been trying for 58 hours to have an armed HVO formation enter Jajce, from the direction of Jajce, with 400 armed soldiers. For the moment, this group was prevented twice by the Muslim forces from moving towards Jajce. This morning I agreed that the representatives of the HVO and SDA should move together with the HVO unit and the armed forces of the TO of BiH in order to resolve the problems that have occurred and in order to ensure our group free passage towards Jajce. You must do everything in your power to resolve the misunderstandings with the Muslims in the area of Novi Travnik and Fojnica and to wield your influence on the Muslims so that we can ensure unimpeded passage towards Jajce." And this was signed together by Slobodan Praljak and Bruno Stojic. Now, in that first portion we see where this order was addressed to, but it reflects the situation and people who feel themselves to be responsible for the situation in Jajce and attempts for forces to reach Jajce. Is that what the document does, it reflects that general situation?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Would you agree with me as well that from this document we can see that everything should be deployed, the HVO and the SDA, that all available resources should be used? Isn't that incompatible, to a certain extent, the HVO and the SDA, but even that was attempted for units to be able to reach Jajce, units which were of a joint composition, you'll agree with me?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prozor was a joint composition too.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I know that you would like to say what you want to say, but would you refrain from that and answer my questions. I'm not talking about Prozor now. I'm not asking you about Prozor, and you haven't come here to answer -- to tell us about the situation in Prozor because you were never in Prozor. Now, I'm asking you about these documents, documents which have to do with your area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This specifically was not in Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And in Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before this period, yes, pursuant to an order from the 3rd Corps commander and I complied with that order.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm -- does this document show that after the 24th you said you had forbidden passage, so up until the 29th, right?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: On several occasions over the past two days you spoke about the following, if I can put it this way, and please correct me if I'm wrong, that Colonel Siljeg was the individual who made the problems and for which -- because of whom the existing conflicts couldn't be resolved. Am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You were shown today -- yes, I can see your answer. Yes. You were shown a document today, and it is P 00840 -- let me just -- may we have it placed on e-court. It is a report from Colonel Miro Andric. I'm sure you will remember it. It is P 00840. I'd like you to see it, because it is a document, as we can see, it is dated the 1st of December, 1992. Now let us take a look at the last paragraph on the second page. May we focus on the last two paragraphs on the second page. Here we have them. Zoom down, please, or pan down. And it says -- a little further up, please. Can we see the document a little further up? He says: "I hereby conclude that Mr. Agic does not wish to implement what we have agreed upon. Because of everything related to the relations and complying with orders given in the area of responsibility set, the problems which surpass my competence and authority, the commander of the armed forces of Gornji Vakuf, Mr. Fahrudin Agic, who, through his promises and signatures, and he does not seem to stand by them, and because he is bypassing the truth does not give us hope that relations within Gornji Vakuf will be solved, or between Gornji Vakuf and Prozor will be solved in a more adequate manner." My question is: Did you know about this weariness expressed by individuals in the HVO towards you?
